propositions: Multiple bundle objects for a single ref cause git to report an ambiguous ref, making the store unclonable and blocking git-remote-s3's push command before any write occurs.
Upstream's git-s3 doctor is interactive-only and discards non-chosen heads, causing permanent data loss of events unique to divergent branches in an append-only event log.

A non-interactive, lossless heal must merge all divergent heads via iterated 2-parent merges (following sync's existing _union_merge semantics), write the merged bundle before deleting originals, and guarantee at least one bundle with full merged history persists after any crash.

The heal acquires the helper's per-ref conditional-put lock, re-enumerates bundles under the lock to avoid TOCTOU, fetches all heads locally, merges them under rebar's write_lock, writes the merged tip as a new bundle object, then deletes the N originals and releases locks.
A real content conflict (same non-derived file edited divergently) must abort the heal without deleting any remote bundle, release locks, and surface fsck-recover, never silently dropping a parent.
Concurrent doctors detect when another process holds the S3 lock and back off without healing, converging on the winning doctor's collapsed single bundle via a subsequent push retry.
